name: The Other Half
opportunity: Women's basketball demand is now durable rather than spiky - three consecutive record seasons, a settled CBA, and event economics verified at the till (A05-S7, A04-S5, A05-S1, A01-S5) - and it is converting into TOPS. The strongest term in the entire cultural dataset is 'female jersey outfit' at +494% (A05-S4), the retail response is jersey-led (A05-S1), and the one Nike women's short with a real willingness-to-pay signal is reportedly worn at home more than on court (A03-S6). The unserved job is therefore NOT a missing women's category - Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, Sabrina 4 Aero-FIT, WNBA Victory and WNBA Rebel Fanwear shorts - it is a women's-block lower half designed, proportioned and MERCHANDISED as the other half of a jersey outfit, in fan and event doors rather than on the performance wall. The move is an occasion retarget and a fixture change, not a new category.
target_consumer: Primary: women and girls 16-35 in the United States who follow the WNBA, Unrivaled and NCAA women's basketball and dress that fandom daily - the buyer who already owns or is buying the jersey and has nothing that belongs with it. She buys in fan doors (Dick's/Foot Locker, WNBAStore/Fanatics, Hibbett), at events (Unrivaled tour stops, All-Star, Final Four), and on Nike's WNBA pages, not on the basketball performance grid. Secondary and explicitly carried rather than assumed: the cross-gender buyer named on the record by Dick's executive chairman Ed Stack in Q1 2026 - 'the basketball business is coming back in a really big fashion and really built around the women's basketball business, whether that's Sabrina, A'ja Wilson,' and 'boys and girls, young men and women are buying that product' (A04-S5). Third: the coverage-first minority inside the same consumer - taller players, modest-dressing athletes - who are not served by a 5-6 inch default (A05-S8). Caution to hold in view: this is exactly the cohort where Nike's own position is weakest - Piper Sandler spring 2025 showed a 13-point drop in female teen mindshare, and fall-2025 coverage attributed the subsequent 'stabilisation' to the MALE upper-income bracket while stating share among girls was still declining (A01-S1).
consumer_problem_jtbd: 'I have the jersey. I have nothing to wear with it that looks like it belongs.' The women's basketball fan completes her game-day and everyday fit from three unrelated places: a licensed replica top, a men's or unisex short bought a size down, and denim. Nike's women's basketball bottoms exist but are cut for play, graded off a performance block, colour-managed to a performance palette, and merchandised on the performance wall - so the short she buys is never the short that matches the jersey she just bought, and it is never in front of her at the moment she buys the top. The job is: complete the outfit, in one fixture, in one transaction, in a proportion that reads as intentional off-court. Evidence that the job is real and currently unserved: 'female jersey outfit' +494% and 'WNBA game outfits' +70% on Pinterest Summer 2026 (A05-S1, A05-S4); Front Office Sports' 'supply desert' framing of the roughly USD 4B US women's sports merchandise market with nearly 80% of respondents saying they would buy more if it existed (Klarna / Sports Innovation Lab, https://frontofficesports.com/womens-sports-merchandise-market-4-billion/, and per that reporting the Indiana Fever and Golden State Valkyries have sold denim shorts and bedazzled shirts successfully - fans will buy lifestyle bottoms, retrieved 2026-09-03); and Nike's own Sabrina reviewers reporting they wear the short at home more often than playing basketball because it is lightweight and comfortable (A03-S6). HYPOTHESIS, not fact: that jersey adjacency is the driver rather than a general athletic-shorts fashion cycle. The Fever/Valkyries denim-shorts datapoint argues the second reading as strongly as the first.
product_idea:
A women's-block fan-and-everyday basketball short, built on ONE new block in TWO inseams, merchandised beside the jersey.

SILHOUETTE: High rise (natural waist, approximately +2.5cm rise over the current Nike women's Dri-FIT basketball grade) with a clean flat front so a jersey tucks without bunching; straight leg with no side-seam taper and a wide hem opening so it hangs rather than clings. This is a proportion decision, not a length decision - the point of difference is rise and leg-line, which is what makes a short read as 'outfit' rather than 'kit'.

INSEAMS: 7 inch and 9 inch only, on the same block, in every colourway. Deliberately NOT a new women's inseam ladder (that would duplicate the rejected A01-O2 framing) and deliberately NOT an extended-length performance tier (that is OPP-08). 7 inch is the graded women's mid; 9 inch reads swingman, photographs as the fan silhouette, and quietly serves the coverage-first consumer (A05-S8, A03-S6) without being marketed as a modesty product.

FABRIC, two faces:
(a) MESH FACE - the volume expression. Double-knit recycled polyester open mesh with a deliberately heavier hand than current performance mesh (target roughly 200-230 g/m2; to be set against the actual Sabrina and DNA GSM files, which nobody in this base has). The fan look wants weight and drape; performance mesh is engineered to be light, and light reads cheap in a fan fixture (A01-S3, A04-S6 seam and 'paper-thin' complaints).
(b) MATTE TRICOT FACE - the going-out expression, with a bound satin-look hem. Same block, different hand.

CONSTRUCTION AND STORAGE: bonded waistband facing for a flat tuck line, internal (not external) drawcord; SYMMETRIC side-seam pockets on both sides with bonded, bartacked pocket bags - this directly fixes the observed defect that the Sabrina reversible carries pockets on one side only (A03-S6); one flat, phone-sized zip security pocket at the back-right yoke, positioned to sit flat under a tucked jersey. Explicitly NOT a cargo or multi-zip utility stack: zip-pocket utility with an 'engineered' wordmark is already Jordan's and adidas' design language (A07-S10). Unlined - this is a fan garment, not a game short. Seam construction and post-wash dimensional stability specified to the OPP-03 'Twenty Washes' standard, but NOT marketed as a durability claim, because the base's durability failure mode is genuinely contested (A01-S3 pockets vs A01-S2/A04-S6 seams and shrinkage).

DETAILS: side-seam trim tape that maps to the jersey's placket trim so the halves visibly belong; tonal woven hem label; optional number-block heat transfer at the left hem for team drops; no visible tech branding on the fan expression.

COLOURWAYS: a four-colour year-round core (black, sail, one team-agnostic bold red, and one treated/sun-faded wash - picking up the 'Treated Color' and 'Sun Faded Dye' expressions A07-S6 surfaced from the internal WNBA brief), plus jersey-matched drops on the jersey calendar (WNBA Rebel Edition in May, All-Star in July), plus one event-exclusive colour per Unrivaled tour stop.

SIZE RUN: XS-3X plus tall from day one, not as a later extension. Nike already carries a plus-size Sabrina SKU (FB8427), so the size architecture exists (A03-S6).

SET SKU: a jersey-plus-short bundle at fan and event doors, which is the merchandising object the whole opportunity actually turns on.

NAMING DIRECTION: 'The Other Half' is the opportunity name, not the product name. Franchise direction: NIKE FULL KIT (short: Full Kit Short) - it names the job, works in translation, and does not over-claim performance. Alternates: COURTSIDE W, and SECOND HALF. Avoid any name that puts it back on the performance wall (no DNA, Icon, Crossover or ISoFly sub-naming) - the naming is part of the fixture argument.
why_now:
Five things converge inside the SS28 window, and one of them cleared a risk the source files were still carrying.

1. Demand durability is now settled, not asserted. The 2026 WNBA season averaged 11,381 across 59 games at the point of measurement - the highest average in league history, ahead of 2025's 10,986 and 2024's 9,807 (https://x.com/scaryman42/status/2060623136081489969 and https://justwomenssports.com/reads/wnba-all-star-game-attendance-record-chicago-united-center-2026/, retrieved 2026-09-03); the All-Star Game drew 19,783 at the United Center, outdrawing the NBA's for the first time (https://ktla.com/news/wnba-all-star-game-record-attendance/); the commissioner called it already the most-watched season of all time at the halfway point, with 73 million unique viewers (https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/wnba-viewership-hits-73-million-200323141.html). That is a third consecutive year of growth, and it happened while Caitlin Clark was sidelined for much of the season - the single-athlete concentration risk has been stress-tested in the field.

2. The labour risk in the source files has cleared. When A04-S5's counter-evidence was written, the CBA had expired 31 Oct 2025 with extensions lapsing. A seven-year CBA covering 2026-2032 has since been ratified, with the 2026 team salary cap set at USD 7.0M, up roughly fivefold, adjusting annually with revenue (https://www.espn.com/wnba/story/_/id/48243808/wnba-cba-2026-collective-bargaining-agreement-news-line-salaries-schedule and https://www.sportspro.com/news/womens-sport/wnba-cba-wnbpa-2032-revenue-salaries-benefits-march-2206/, retrieved 2026-09-03). A line planned to a women's basketball calendar now has a seven-year calendar.

3. Event retail is proven at the till, in one night, with a number. Unrivaled's Philadelphia tour stop on 30 Jan 2026 drew 21,490 - a professional women's regular-season record - generating roughly USD 1M in tickets and USD 400,000 in merchandise, over USD 2M total in a single night (A05-S7; https://www.inquirer.com/wnba/unrivaled-philadelphia-womens-basketball-attendance-record-20260131.html and https://www.unrivaled.basketball/news/unrivaled-numbers-in-season-2-2xxhf3n3q35f, retrieved 2026-09-03). Ticket revenue rose 204% and tickets sold 249% season over season. This is the instrument that makes the whole idea cheap to test.

4. The aesthetic has a second, independent instrument beyond the Pinterest data. Track and basketball shorts appeared on Spring/Summer 2026 runways at Fendi, No. 21, Lacoste and Onitsuka Tiger and are being styled as everyday women's wear by named figures (https://www.marieclaire.com/fashion/celebrity-style/track-shorts-trend-summer-2026-styling/, retrieved 2026-09-03). Two seasons of continuity across two unrelated instruments is the reason this survives the hype-vs-sustained test that the retro-swingman thesis fails (audit: hype_vs_sustained).

5. The channel is swinging toward exactly the doors this product needs. Nike wholesale grew 4% in Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital fell for a tenth consecutive quarter (A02-S7); Dick's now owns Foot Locker and its executive chairman publicly attributed a basketball recovery to women's basketball across BOTH banners (A04-S5). A fan-fixture product built for wholesale sell-through is aligned with where Nike's volume is actually moving. And the SS28 season contains LA28, opening 14 July 2028 in Nike's home market - the largest women's-basketball visibility moment of the cycle, and absent from all seven source files (audit: geographic_bias).

key_features_benefits.feature: One women's-specific block with a raised rise and a straight, untapered leg - a proportion change, not a length change
key_features_benefits.benefit: Makes the short read as deliberate off-court and lets a jersey tuck flat, which is the styling move the whole occasion is built on. It also removes the 'size up if you typically wear men's styles' logic without inventing a new inseam ladder.

key_features_benefits.feature: Two inseams (7 inch and 9 inch) in every colourway on the same block, XS-3X plus tall from day one
key_features_benefits.benefit: Serves the fan silhouette and the coverage-first consumer from one pattern and one costing, and does it without a modesty label. Nike already carries a plus-size Sabrina SKU (FB8427), so the size architecture is proven rather than speculative.

key_features_benefits.feature: Jersey-matched colour and side-seam trim, dropped on the jersey calendar (Rebel Edition May, All-Star July, one exclusive per Unrivaled tour stop)
key_features_benefits.benefit: Converts a top purchase into a two-piece purchase at the moment of the top purchase. This is the actual mechanism of the opportunity: the halves have to match and they have to be in the same fixture.

key_features_benefits.feature: Heavier-hand mesh face (target roughly 200-230 g/m2) with drape, plus a matte tricot alternative on the same block
key_features_benefits.benefit: Fan bottoms are judged by hand and hang, not by weight savings. It also directly answers the 'paper-thin' and post-wash complaints in the value-channel review corpus without making a durability claim the evidence cannot support.

key_features_benefits.feature: Symmetric bonded, bartacked side pockets on BOTH sides, plus one flat back-yoke zip security pocket
key_features_benefits.benefit: Fixes the specific, verified defect that the Sabrina reversible carries pockets on one side only, and gives a phone a flat home under a tucked jersey - without adopting the cargo/multi-zip 'engineered' language Jordan and adidas already own.

key_features_benefits.feature: Merchandised in fan and event fixtures adjacent to the jersey - Nike WNBA pages, WNBAStore/Fanatics, Dick's and Foot Locker fan walls, Hibbett, and event retail - not on the basketball performance grid
key_features_benefits.benefit: This is the change that costs the least and is most likely to be the whole answer. Nike already has women's basketball bottoms; the evidence that they are in the wrong fixture is stronger than any evidence that they are the wrong product.

key_features_benefits.feature: Jersey-plus-short set SKU at fan and event doors
key_features_benefits.benefit: Raises transaction value at exactly the moment and place where the highest-intent buyer is standing, and produces the category-split data that currently does not exist anywhere.

key_features_benefits.feature: Recycled and textile-to-textile content held as a compliance baseline with EmpCo-compliant claim language, never as the lead claim
key_features_benefits.benefit: Every competitor already claims 70-100% recycled, so the percentage no longer sells; but the EU Empowering Consumers Directive applies from 27 September 2026, so the hangtag is now a legal exposure for anything sold in Europe.

target_price.msrp: USD 65 core (7 inch and 9 inch, mesh and tricot faces); USD 75 for jersey-matched team and Rebel Edition drops; set SKU (jersey + short) at a modest bundle discount to the sum of parts
target_price.tier: Premium-core fan/lifestyle. Explicitly NOT a performance rung and explicitly NOT an innovation rung - the price is argued from occasion and comparison set, not from a feature.
target_price.rationale:
Read this against the audit's standing warning first: three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexist in the source base, none of them from a retrieved page, and the audit's instruction is that no price in any opportunity should be treated as a recommendation until Nike's internal list-vs-realised ASP is pulled. The prices below are anchors, not a recommendation.

The observed women's Nike basketball rung is USD 65: Sabrina Dri-FIT short at USD 65 with a plus-size SKU (A03-S6), Women's Crossover Dri-FIT 5 inch at USD 65 regular seen at USD 52.97 (A03-S6). My own check on 2026-09-03 returned the Sabrina Dri-FIT Reversible at USD 42.97 from a USD 65 regular price (nike.com via search summary, https://www.nike.com/w/womens-basketball-shorts-38fphz3glsmz5e1x6) - i.e. the USD 65 rung is already clearing at roughly a third off. That is the single most important price fact here and it cuts AGAINST holding USD 65 on feature alone.

The argument for USD 65-75 is therefore the comparison set, not the product. In the fan fixture the neighbours are higher: Mitchell & Ness WNBA women's swingman shorts at USD 80 (https://www.mitchellandness.com/en/wnba/shorts/o-3604+d-31990174+z-99332-2852334060, search summary, retrieved 2026-09-03) and Nike's own WNBA fanwear knee-length short reported at USD 85 (https://www.nike.com/w/wnba-clothing-6ef6nz6ymx6, search summary, retrieved 2026-09-03 - NOT confirmed against a retrieved page and to be treated as unverified). On the performance wall the neighbours are lower: the DNA ladder runs roughly USD 37-65 with the longest inseam cheapest. Moving the short into the fan fixture is what makes USD 65-75 arguable at all; leaving it on the performance wall makes USD 50 the ceiling.

Two structural pressures argue the other way and must be shown to the Council. Nike apparel grew on ASP mix rather than pricing power in FY2026 (apparel USD 13.4B, +2% currency-neutral, units +1%, ASP contributing about 1 point, and that ASP lift already partially offset by higher discounts and channel mix) - there is no rising tide to price into (A03-S9). And the US marketplace turned increasingly promotional through summer 2026, with Sabrina tees already marked to USD 15.97-28.97 at Dick's (A04-S4, A04-S5). Note also that A04-S8's 'everything under USD 100 is frozen' premise is superseded: Nike has since taken surgical increases of about +3% on apparel against a tariff headwind revised to roughly USD 1.5B and 120bp (audit contradiction: 'Nike's shorts prices are frozen under USD 100').

Given all of that, the honest position is: USD 65 core / USD 75 drop is a hypothesis to be tested at full price for eight weeks in a fan fixture before it is a plan, and it should be costed so that it survives at USD 55 if it does not hold.
target_price.regional_notes: United States is the lead and, on this evidence, the only defensible launch market: roughly 48% of surviving signals are US-primary and closer to 70% once US-derived 'Global' signals are attributed (audit: geographic_bias). Australia is the one credible second market - about 1.3M players, female participation +25% since 2022, NBL total attendance 1,093,048, and an on-court league partner (Champion) that is not a performance-basketball leader, with Rebel/JD/Foot Locker doors open (A02-S9); index AUD to the US rung. Europe would carry roughly EUR 65-75 / GBP 55-65 but has literally no signal in this base where it is the primary market, and any claim language must clear the EU Empowering Consumers Directive from 27 September 2026 (A03-S5). Greater China should be excluded at launch and this should be stated plainly rather than hedged: Nike Greater China fell 13% currency-neutral in FY26 with apparel units -8%, and Topsports - Nike's largest Greater China retail partner - stops selling Nike online by January 2027, which breaks the route to market (A02-S2, A04-S2, audit). There is not one Chinese price observation anywhere in the base. Nothing in this opportunity serves the Worldball priority space, and it should not be sold to the Council as if it does.

market_distribution_role:
ROLE IN LINE: a seasonal fan-bottoms programme with a two-season path to franchise status, sitting deliberately OUTSIDE the basketball performance line plan. It is the lower half of the jersey business, not a rung on the shorts ladder. It should be planned against the licensed/fanwear P&L, bought by the fan buyer, and reviewed against jersey attach rate rather than against DNA or Sabrina sell-through.

LEAD MARKET: United States. Second market: Australia (A02-S9). Europe as a fast-follow with EmpCo-compliant claim language. Greater China excluded at launch (A02-S2, A04-S2).

CHANNEL MIX, wholesale-weighted and deliberately so: roughly 55-60% wholesale (Dick's and Foot Locker under one owner, Hibbett, Fanatics/WNBAStore), 25-30% Nike Direct but placed on the WNBA and fan pages rather than the basketball performance grid, and 10-15% event retail (Unrivaled tour stops, WNBA All-Star, NCAA Final Four, Portland Fire and Golden State Valkyries arena retail). The weighting follows the evidence, not preference: Nike Digital has now declined for ten consecutive quarters while wholesale grew 4% in Q4 and full-year FY26, and retailers - not Nike.com - are the shorts merchants in this category (A02-S7).

LAUNCH CADENCE: build the buy around jersey moments, not apparel seasons. Rebel Edition drops land in May; All-Star in July; the Unrivaled tour stop calendar runs January-March. That gives three in-season drop windows a year plus a four-colour year-round core. SS28 delivery lands in the LA28 build-up (Games open 14 July 2028, in the US), which is the largest women's-basketball visibility moment in the cycle and appears nowhere in the seven source files (audit: geographic_bias).

FIXTURE, which is the actual ask: the product must be merchandised adjacent to the jersey - same wall, same size run, ideally the same hanger for the set SKU. If the fixture change cannot be secured with Dick's/Foot Locker, the product should not be made, because the fixture IS the opportunity. Nike already sells women's basketball shorts; what it does not sell is a short standing next to the jersey it matches.

SEQUENCING: run the USD 40-60k test first (Unrivaled category split plus a live SKU-and-fixture audit) before any tooling or block development. This is the cheapest decisive test in the portfolio and it can be run in weeks.

evidence_stack.contribution: Supplies the demand shape and the test instrument. A05-S7 is the load-bearing item and is VERIFIED: Unrivaled expanded a year early, 2026 ticket revenue +204% and tickets sold +249%, a professional women's regular-season record crowd of 21,490 in Philadelphia, and - the datapoint the specialist missed and the skeptic found - roughly USD 1M in tickets and USD 400,000 in merchandise from that one night. That single number is both the commercial proof for event retail and the cheapest available test of this entire thesis, because splitting it by category (jersey vs tee vs bottoms) settles the question directly. A05-S1 supplies the Pinterest conversion behaviour ('female jersey outfit' +494%, 'WNBA game outfits' +70%) and the Front Office Sports 'supply desert' framing. A05-S4 supplies the wide-cut, sport-as-identity aesthetic and, critically, also supplies this opportunity's biggest contradiction. A05-S8 supplies the coverage-first minority that justifies the 9 inch inseam.

Supplies the pivot. A03-S6's own skeptic counter-evidence is the most important single line in this opportunity: Sabrina reviewers report wearing the short at home more often than playing basketball because it is lightweight and comfortable, which means the USD 65 willingness-to-pay Nike has already proven is being paid partly for a LIFESTYLE occasion. That reframes the whole women's-shorts question from 'build better performance construction' to 'serve the occasion people are already using the product for.' A03-S6 also supplies the verified reversible one-side-pocket defect, the plus-size SKU FB8427, and the fact that a women's 5 inch Crossover already exists at USD 65 - which is what stops this becoming another 'the category is empty' claim. A03-S9 (FY2026 apparel USD 13.4B, +2% cn, units +1%, ASP contributing ~1 point) is the pricing discipline: no rising tide, so a new short must earn a NEW occasion. A03-S4 and A03-S5 set the innovation and compliance boundaries.

Supplies the first-party retailer demand call-out, which is the strongest non-Nike commercial evidence in the base. What survives A04-S5 after the audit strips its numbers is better than the numbers were: Ed Stack on the Dick's Q1 2026 call saying the basketball business is coming back built around women's basketball, naming Sabrina and A'ja Wilson, and describing the buyer as 'boys and girls, young men and women' - a senior, dated, first-party demand statement across both Dick's and Foot Locker banners, describing cross-gender fan demand rather than player demand. A04-S4 supplies the promotional floor this product must clear (Foot Locker comps -3.6%, 'increasingly promotional'). A04-S8 supplies the margin condition, with the correction that its price-freeze premise is superseded by Nike's subsequent ~+3% apparel increases.

Supplies the channel architecture, which is what turns this from a design idea into a merchandising plan. A02-S7 is VERIFIED: Nike wholesale +4% in Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter, with retailers (Foot Locker, Dick's, Fanatics/NBA Store, Titan 22, Rebel, KICKZ) identified as the actual shorts merchants and an explicit conclusion that shorts line plans should be built for wholesale sell-through rather than app-exclusive drops. It also carries the Jordan Streetwear over-distribution warning, which is the relevant cautionary tale for a lifestyle-coded basketball bottom. A02-S9 is the only registry-grade non-US market evidence in the entire base and the reason Australia is the named second market: ~1.3M players, female participation +25% since 2022, NBL attendance 1,093,048, and a league apparel partner that is not a performance-basketball leader.

Supplies the consumer-side corroboration and the uncomfortable counterweight. A01-S5's qualitative half is, per its own skeptic, the strongest item in that file and the one that survived the hype-vs-sustained test: the basketball/athletic short as a women's fashion object, corroborated a full year past the original Who What Wear piece by summer-2026 coverage with named adoption - two seasons of continuity, not a moment. Its quantitative half is struck (the +60% is a mis-transcription of the published +601%, and both it and the Circana figures in A01-S6 trace to one Substack guest post). A01-S1 is the counterweight and belongs in the Council conversation: the female teen mindshare Nike lost is precisely this consumer, Nike's teen APPAREL mindshare is 26% not 49%, and share among girls was still declining as of fall 2025.

Supplies the design vocabulary and, honestly, the weakest evidence in the stack. A07-S6 contributes the treated-colour and sun-faded-dye expressions from the internal WNBA brief and the texture-led surface direction, plus the observation that custom uniform size charts default women to 6 inch with 5 inch on request - a manufacturing convention, not consumer preference. Its central claim, that women's basketball shorts are unisex or licensed generics, does NOT survive and this opportunity does not rely on it: Nike put Aero-FIT on a women's-athlete-led signature short and jersey first, before the rest of basketball (Sabrina 4, 17 July 2026). A07-S10 contributes a negative constraint that shapes the product: zip-pocket utility with an 'engineered' wordmark is already owned by Jordan and adidas, so this short must not compete there.

contradictory_evidence.description: THE CENTRAL CONTRADICTION, AND IT POINTS AT TOPS. The strongest term in the dataset is 'female jersey outfit' at +494% - a JERSEY term. The culture domain used jersey-search growth as proof that consumers want shorts; the more direct reading is that it is proof consumers want jerseys, and that the retail supply chain being jersey-led (A05-S1) is a rational response rather than a failure. This opportunity survives that reading only if you accept that an 'outfit' search implies a second garment, which is an inference, not an observation. It is not proven anywhere in this base.

THE ATTRIBUTION IS PAN-SPORT, NOT BASKETBALL. The same Pinterest Summer 2026 report shows 'Formula 1 aesthetic outfit' +483% and 'Brazil jersey outfit women' +302%, growing as fast or faster than the WNBA terms. Sport-as-fashion is broad; attributing it to basketball is correlation-as-causation and would misdirect a basketball-specific line. Compounding this: Pinterest is a platform search-and-save index on a female-skewing pinboard, not purchase behaviour, and the percentages are growth rates with no absolute base disclosed - a +494% on a tiny base is not a market. This is carried openly in the synthesis and should be carried openly to the Council.

ONE PRESS RELEASE COUNTED THREE TIMES. The +601% (WNBAStore.com plus NYC flagship), +233% (Dick's) and Fanatics 5x figures that quantify the women's opportunity in three domains all derive from a single WNBA marketing document - 'WNBA Delivers Record-Setting 2024 Season', September 2024, measured against a pre-Caitlin-Clark 2023 base - arriving through three different laundering paths, including Accio (an Alibaba AI B2B sourcing engine) in A04-S5's case, where it was also mis-dated to 2025. A01-S5 renders the +601% as +60%, an order-of-magnitude transcription error. Per the audit, count it once, strip the numbers, and replace with 2026 figures on an explicit base year. What survives from A04-S5 is the Ed Stack quote, which is stronger than the numbers were.

THE ATTENDANCE HEADLINE IS PARTLY A SCHEDULE ARTEFACT. The 2025 +34% is mostly the schedule expanding from roughly 240 games to 286 (a 44-game season plus the Valkyries); per-game attendance moved from about 9,790 to about 11,014, roughly +13%. The specialist's quoted 11,148 average also conflicts with its own cited source (10,954 SportsPro / 10,986 Wikipedia). The direction survives - 2026 is a third consecutive record on a per-game basis - but the growth rate that made the case exciting is roughly a third of what was presented.

THE INCUMBENT MAY ALREADY SERVE THE JOB. The Sabrina at-home-wear reviews are this opportunity's key evidence AND its sharpest counter-argument: if buyers are already paying USD 65 for a Nike women's basketball short to wear off-court, the lifestyle occasion is being served today by product that exists, and the only thing missing is the fixture. That would make the correct action a merchandising change costing near-zero, not a new block. Separately, A07-S6's 'women's shorts are unisex or licensed generics' framing is false: Nike put Aero-FIT on a women's-athlete-led signature short and jersey FIRST (Sabrina 4, 17 July 2026), ships a women's 5 inch Crossover at USD 65, a plus-size Sabrina (FB8427), WNBA Victory and WNBA Rebel Fanwear shorts (May 2026), and the Caitlin Clark line including shorts at retail from 1 October 2026. Any version of this idea that reads as 'the women's category is empty' should be rejected on audit, and this one is deliberately written not to.

THE PRICE MAY NOT HOLD. The US athletic marketplace turned increasingly promotional through summer 2026 (Ed Stack's own words; Foot Locker comps -3.6% with the FY outlook cut; Nike citing elevated promotions and markdowns). Sabrina tees are already marked to USD 15.97-28.97 at Dick's, and my own 2026-09-03 check returned the Sabrina Dri-FIT Reversible short at USD 42.97 from a USD 65 regular price. Meanwhile Nike apparel units grew 1% in FY2026 with ASP doing the rest, and that ASP lift came from product mix and was already partially offset by higher discounts and channel mix. A new USD 65-75 women's fan bottom is being proposed into a fixture where the adjacent Nike women's short is clearing at a third off.

EVERY PRICE IN THIS DOCUMENT IS UNANCHORED, INCLUDING MINE. The audit is explicit: three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexist in the base, not one of them from a retrieved page, and no price in any opportunity should be treated as a recommendation until Nike's internal list-vs-realised ASP and markdown rate by inseam are pulled. My own web checks on 2026-09-03 (Mitchell & Ness WNBA women's swingman at USD 80; Nike WNBA fanwear knee-length at USD 85; Sabrina Reversible at USD 42.97 from USD 65) are search-result summaries, not retrieved product pages, and the USD 85 figure in particular should be treated as unverified. Additionally, A04-S8's 'all product under USD 100 is price-frozen' premise is superseded: Nike has taken surgical increases of about +3% on apparel against a tariff headwind revised to roughly USD 1.5B and 120bp.

NIKE IS WEAKEST WITH EXACTLY THIS CONSUMER. Piper Sandler spring 2025 showed a 13-point drop in Nike mindshare among female teens, with female share under 40% for the first time since 2020. The skeptic's correction makes it worse for this opportunity, not better: the widely-quoted 49% is Nike's FOOTWEAR mindshare, while APPAREL mindshare is 26% (Hollister 12%, Brandy Melville 6%), and fall-2025 coverage attributes the 'stabilisation' specifically to the MALE upper-income bracket while stating that share among girls is still declining. The spring 2026 survey exists and was never consulted. Right to win is not the same as current standing.

THE TEST INSTRUMENT IS A TWO-SEASON STARTUP LEAGUE, AND THE EVIDENCE BASE IS ONE COUNTRY. Unrivaled is two seasons old, so a one-season viewership dip against a novelty-inflated debut is a thin basis for the word 'decoupling', and whether its event-retail pattern generalises to the WNBA is untested. More broadly, roughly 48% of surviving signals are US-primary and closer to 70% once US-derived 'Global' signals are attributed; Europe is the primary market of exactly zero signals, Latin America of none. This opportunity is a US idea with one Australian data point, being written into a global SS28 line whose stated priority spaces include Worldball and Greater China. It serves Women's Revolution and does not serve Worldball at all - and it should be presented that way rather than stretched.

confidence_rationale:
61 reflects a genuine split: the demand half is among the best-evidenced things in the entire portfolio, and the product half is a hypothesis with one supporting datapoint.

What pushes it up. Women's basketball demand durability is now settled rather than argued - three consecutive record seasons on a per-game basis, a 2026 All-Star crowd that outdrew the NBA's, 73 million unique viewers at the halfway point, and a seven-year CBA ratified with the team cap at USD 7.0M. This is the one place in the whole audit where new evidence made a signal STRONGER rather than weaker, and the concentration risk was stress-tested in the field when the league grew with Caitlin Clark sidelined for much of 2026. Four independent instruments agree on the shape (A05-S7 event economics, A04-S5 a first-party retailer call-out, A02-S9 registry participation in a second country, A01-S1 a large teen panel). The aesthetic has two unrelated instruments across two seasons (Pinterest, and SS26 runway plus editorial adoption). The channel logic is verified rather than inferred (A02-S7). And the opportunity is deliberately built to survive the audit's most common failure mode: it does not claim the category is empty, because Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, Sabrina 4 Aero-FIT, WNBA Victory and WNBA Rebel Fanwear shorts, and the Caitlin Clark line lands 1 October 2026.

What holds it down, and holds it below 70. The pivotal inference - that jersey-outfit search behaviour implies demand for a matching BOTTOM - is not observed anywhere. The strongest term in the base is a jersey term, and the same report shows F1 and Brazil-football terms growing as fast or faster, so the basketball attribution is not supported by A05-S4. The single best product-side datapoint (Sabrina worn at home) is a handful of reviews, and it cuts both ways: it is the evidence for the occasion retarget AND the evidence that the incumbent product already serves it, which would make the right answer a fixture change costing nothing rather than a new block. There is no shorts-level unit, sell-through, ASP or markdown data anywhere in the base, in any geography, split by gender or otherwise, so the price is unanchored by the audit's own explicit instruction. The nearest observable price is a Nike women's short at USD 65 clearing at USD 42.97 into an increasingly promotional US marketplace. And Nike's standing with this specific consumer is measurably eroding, not improving.

What keeps it from going lower is that the decisive test is unusually cheap and fast: split the Unrivaled Philadelphia USD 400,000 by category and run a live SKU-and-fixture audit. Roughly USD 40-60k and a few weeks either licenses this or kills it. That asymmetry - high demand certainty, low product certainty, near-zero cost to resolve - is what a 61 should mean.
what_would_need_to_be_true: Bottoms are a materially non-trivial share of women's basketball fan merchandise, not a rounding error. Concrete threshold: split the Unrivaled Philadelphia USD 400,000 merchandise night (30 January 2026) by category - jersey vs tee vs headwear vs bottoms - and require bottoms to exceed roughly 12% of units. If the night was 90%+ tops, the correct read is A05-S4's literal one (the demand is for jerseys) and this opportunity should be killed rather than reshaped.

The gap is fixture and adjacency, not assortment. A live SKU-and-door audit must show that Nike's existing women's basketball bottoms (ISoFly 6.5/7 inch, Crossover 5 inch, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, Sabrina 4, WNBA Victory, WNBA Rebel Fanwear) sit on the performance grid and are NOT merchandised adjacent to the jersey in fan and event doors. If they are already adjacent and still not selling, the thesis is wrong.

Nike's internal split of women's basketball revenue into fan/jersey versus performance bottoms shows the fan side materially under-bottomed relative to tops - with size-curve fill and rebuy by door, and with 2026 WNBA Rebel Fanwear short sell-through as the direct read. This is the single pull that resolves the most of this opportunity and Nike already owns it.

A USD 65-75 fan rung holds at full price for at least eight consecutive weeks in a fan fixture, against a Sabrina rung currently clearing at USD 42.97 and a marketplace Ed Stack described as increasingly promotional. If it clears below USD 55 in week four, the product must be re-costed to survive at USD 55 or dropped.

A women's high-rise, straight-leg block outperforms the current women's grade on the OUTFIT occasion specifically - tested on n>=200 women 16-35 who own a women's basketball jersey, evaluating rise, leg-line and hang with a jersey tucked, not on-court fit. The 105-athlete WNBA council focus groups A07 points to should be mined for rise and waistband preference first.

Dick's and Foot Locker (one owner since 2026) will actually take a women's basketball bottom into a non-performance fan fixture and hold it there for a full season. Without the fixture commitment this product is a normal short in the wrong place, and it should not be tooled.

The basketball terms carry real absolute volume, not just growth rate. Obtain the underlying Pinterest term list ranked by absolute volume and compare the WNBA/basketball terms against the F1 and football terms on the same base. If basketball is a small absolute base growing fast alongside larger pan-sport bases, the aesthetic belongs to sport generally and Nike should build it in football or as a Sportswear programme instead.
what_we_still_dont_know: Whether ANY of the Pinterest percentages sit on a meaningful absolute base. The audit's instruction is explicit and unmet: get the term list ranked by absolute volume, because a +494% on a tiny base is not a market. Nobody in seven domains has that number.

Anything at all about basketball shorts unit volumes, sell-through, realised ASP, markdown rate, size-curve fill, return rate or return reasons - in any geography, at any inseam, for either gender. The audit is unambiguous that no first-party Nike commercial data exists anywhere in the base, which is why every price and every length in every opportunity in this portfolio is unanchored.

Whether the behaviour is jersey-adjacency or general athletic-shorts fashion. If it is the latter, the buyer will pair the jersey with any short she likes and a jersey-matched bottom earns no premium - a reading actively supported by the Front Office Sports report that the Indiana Fever and Golden State Valkyries have sold DENIM shorts and bedazzled shirts successfully, which is a fan-lifestyle purchase with no performance or matching logic at all.

Whether the WNBA Rebel Fanwear short (May 2026) sold. It is the closest thing to a live in-market test of this exact idea, Nike owns the number, and it appears in no file. If it sold, the case is largely made; if it did not, the case is largely broken.

Who the buyer actually is. Ed Stack described 'boys and girls, young men and women' buying women's basketball product. If the volume buyer is materially cross-gender, a women's-specific block is the wrong construction decision and the answer is a unisex fan block in a women's size run - the opposite product from the same evidence.
Whether the Unrivaled event-retail pattern generalises to the WNBA, or is specific to a two-season startup league running a novelty tour-stop format in NBA arenas.

Europe, entirely. Nike's second geography is the primary market of zero signals in this base. EuroLeague set a fourth consecutive attendance record in 2025-26 (3.25 million, +8%, TV viewership +82% to 122.8 million) and none of it is in any file; whether European women's basketball fandom converts to apparel the same way is completely unmeasured.

The actual GSM of the current Nike women's basketball shorts and whether the 200-230 g/m2 heavier-hand target is a real change or a description of what is already shipping. Nobody has established that fabric weight changed at all, in either direction, on any Nike shorts franchise.
nike_right_to_win:
Nike owns the top. It designs and supplies the WNBA on-court uniform, including the 2026 Rebel Edition programme that let teams express their own identity; it holds the two established women's basketball signature lines (Sabrina, A'ja Wilson) and adds a third with Caitlin Clark at retail from 1 October 2026; and it put Aero-FIT - its most advanced cooling platform, claimed at more than double the airflow of legacy Nike apparel - onto a women's-athlete-led signature short and jersey FIRST, before the rest of basketball, on 17 July 2026 (A03-S4, and the counter-evidence to A07-S6). If the job to be done is literally 'the other half of a Nike jersey,' then only Nike can make the halves match: it controls the trim, the placket, the colour standard and the drop calendar on both garments. Mitchell & Ness owns the retro fan bottom at USD 80 but has no current on-court top to match. Fanatics distributes at scale (5x WNBA merchandise year over year) but does not design the block. adidas and Puma have women's basketball bottoms and, in Puma's case, a named creative director for women's basketball (June Ambrose, A07-S6), but neither holds the WNBA on-court licence.

The channel fits too. The volume is swinging to exactly the doors this product needs - Nike wholesale grew 4% in Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter (A02-S7) - and the retailer that now owns both Dick's and Foot Locker has publicly and specifically attributed a basketball recovery to women's basketball across both banners (A04-S5). Nike is asking for a fixture from a partner that has already said on an earnings call that this is what is selling.

The honest weakness, and it should be said out loud in the Council: Nike's standing with this exact consumer is the number that is falling. Teen female mindshare dropped 13 points in spring 2025, Nike's teen APPAREL mindshare is 26% rather than the widely-quoted 49% footwear figure, and share among girls was still declining as of fall 2025 while stabilisation came from upper-income boys (A01-S1). Nike's right to win here is structural - it owns the jersey - not relational. It is a licence position and a supply-chain position, not evidence that this consumer currently prefers Nike.

narrative:
This spec was built by reading one dataset against the conclusion its own domain drew from it.

The culture domain used Pinterest's Summer 2026 numbers as proof that women want basketball shorts. But the strongest term in that report is 'female jersey outfit' at +494% - a jersey term - and the retail response the same signal describes is jersey-led. Read literally, the data argues for tops - which should have ended the idea. What kept it alive was a line buried in a skeptic's counter-evidence in a different file: Sabrina reviewers report wearing the short at home more often than playing basketball. Nike has therefore already proven a USD 65 willingness-to-pay for a women's basketball short - for the wrong occasion, in the wrong fixture. Put that next to a number the culture specialist missed and its skeptic found - USD 400,000 of merchandise in one night in Philadelphia - and the shape changes. The demand is not for a category Nike lacks. It is for an adjacency Nike does not merchandise.

The hardest call was resisting the version the evidence keeps pulling toward. Three domains read one 2024 WNBA press release and concluded the women's category was empty. It is not: Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, Sabrina 4 with Aero-FIT, WNBA Victory and WNBA Rebel Fanwear shorts, plus a plus-size SKU, with the Caitlin Clark line landing 1 October 2026. Any brief saying women have no basketball shorts dies on audit, correctly. So this had to stay narrow: not a new category, not a new inseam ladder (that is OPP-08), not a team-identity fan short (Nike shipped one in May 2026). Only block, rise, proportion, and where it hangs in the store.

What I argued with myself about most was whether it should be a product at all. If Sabrina buyers already wear the incumbent for this occasion, the minimal honest action is to move existing product next to the jersey and watch - a merchandising change costing near zero. I kept the block because rise and leg-line are what make a short read as an outfit rather than as kit, and a performance grade cannot be styled into that. The sequencing reflects the doubt: test before tooling.

The second argument was price, and I lost it as much as I won it. The audit says no price in this portfolio is anchored - three incompatible Nike ladders, none from a retrieved page - and my own checks were search summaries, not pages. The most useful thing I found argues against my own number: Nike's Sabrina reversible, at the exact rung I am proposing, showed at USD 42.97 against a USD 65 list. So USD 65-75 is not a recommendation. It survives only if the fixture changes the comparison set from a USD 37-65 performance wall to a USD 80-85 fan wall, and it must be costed to live at USD 55 if it does not.

Worth stating plainly what this is not. It is a US idea with one Australian datapoint, in a base roughly seventy percent US. It serves Women's Revolution; it does not serve Worldball, and Greater China should be excluded at launch. Stretching it to cover a space it does not cover would repeat the source files' own error.

What makes it worth a Council slot anyway is the asymmetry. Demand certainty is high and durable across three seasons and a signed CBA; product certainty is low; and the test separating them is the cheapest in the portfolio: split one night's merchandise receipts by category, and audit where the existing shorts hang.
